AI ANALYSIS

Data-Driven Betting Insights

Ludvig Aberg towers over this Charles Schwab Challenge field with a massive +2.04 SG Total and an 8.8% model win probability — more than double the next closest competitor — making him the clear alpha play at +1039. Below him, a cluster of value emerges in the +3000 to +4000 range: J.J. Spaun ranks #3 in overall strokes gained (+1.27) and #2 in SG Approach (+0.83) at +3547, while Ben Griffin — the defending champion — leads the field in putting (+0.56 SG Putting) and carries a 3.2% model win probability at +3068. With Colonial Country Club rewarding precision ball-striking and putting on small, undulating greens, this week's data points to a clear hierarchy of value plays beneath Aberg's dominance.
Aberg Is the Unquestioned Top Dog
Ludvig Aberg's +2.04 SG Total leads the field by a staggering 0.68 strokes over the next-best player, and his 8.8% model win probability dwarfs the implied 0.1% from his +1039 odds. He also ranks #1 in SG Approach at +0.86 — a critical skill at Colonial's tight, demanding approach shots.
Ludvig Aberg
J.J. Spaun: Elite Ball-Striker at Value Odds
Spaun ranks #3 in SG Total (+1.27) and #2 in SG Approach (+0.83), yet his +3547 odds imply far less than his 2.7% model win probability. After a T6 finish here in 2025, he has proven he can contend at Colonial when he avoids the cut — a boom-or-bust profile worth backing at this price.
J.J. Spaun
Defending Champ Griffin Leads in Putting
Ben Griffin won this event in 2025 and leads the entire field in SG Putting at +0.56. His model win probability of 3.2% and +1.17 SG Total make him a legitimate contender at +3068, and his course history adjustment confirms his comfort level at Colonial.
Ben Griffin
Russell Henley Offers Best Risk-Reward
Henley's +1.36 SG Total ranks #2 in the field and his 4.3% model win probability is the second-highest, yet he sits at +2247. He also ranks #5 in SG Approach (+0.53) and carries the best course fit adjustment among top contenders at +0.124, making him the most compelling outright value play on the board.
Russell Henley
Harry Hall Is the Primo Longshot
At +5576, Harry Hall boasts a +0.90 SG Total (better than some players 50 spots shorter in odds), ranks #5 in SG Putting (+0.46), and carries a 16.1% top-10 probability. That top-10 number makes him a strong each-way or top-10 market play alongside his outright price.
Harry Hall
Keegan Bradley: Hidden SG Profile at +5456
Bradley's +0.86 SG Total matches players priced 20-30 spots shorter, and his 15.4% top-10 probability suggests he's being overlooked at +5456. Colonial's emphasis on accuracy and course management plays into his veteran skill set, making him a sneaky contender.
Keegan Bradley
MacIntyre Pairs Putter with Recent Form
Robert MacIntyre ranks #3 in SG Putting (+0.49) and #5 in SG Total (+1.25), with a T6 here in 2025 showing he's figured out Colonial. His 2.8% model win probability offers clear edge against his +3491 price, and his well-rounded game suits a course that demands no weaknesses.
Robert MacIntyre
Justin Thomas: Big Name, Real Value
Thomas sits at #4 in SG Total (+1.25) with a 3.2% model win probability, yet +3017 odds significantly underrate his chances. While his -0.036 course fit is slightly negative, his elite ball-striking pedigree and comfort on tight, traditional courses make him a worthy play at this number.
Justin Thomas
Bud Cauley: Best Top-10 Probability Among Longshots
Cauley's 16.2% top-10 probability leads all longshots at +5345 or longer, backed by a solid +0.75 SG Total. He's a top-10/top-20 market specialist at this price point, and his accuracy-first game maps well to Colonial's narrow fairways.
Bud Cauley
Smalley's Course History Raises Red Flags
Despite ranking #7 in SG Total (+1.17), Alex Smalley has a missed cut and a withdrawal in his last two trips to Colonial and a slightly negative course fit (-0.016). At +3892, there are better options in this range like Spaun and MacIntyre who have proven they can perform here.
Alex Smalley
